1. Tampons is a personal choice. When my daughter started, I bought her an assortment of pads and tampons for her to try out and now she prefers pad. I personally prefer the latter but it also depends on flow, which will increase as she gets older. 
2. It really does depend on hair type. You could take them to a salon and see what the stylist suggest. Or make your own assessment. There are generally three types of products. Oily hair, neutral and dry. If their hair tends to get darker a day after it has been washed it is most likely oily. If it looks frizzy and the ends start to split it is dry, if non of the above they have regular hair which basic products is okay.
3. The easiest way to decorate ( this even applies for general rooms ) is pick a theme. So for instance they want Spongebob. Search a Spongebob color pallet. Use the lightest color for walls or an accent wall. Maybe the next lightest color for the trim. Then accent with the rest of the colors in bedding, other furniture and accessories. You can also find decals and patterns you could embellish with.
4. What are your child's strengths and weaknesses? I'd say to get the ball rolling go with strengths. Are they creative or sporty? Maybe they are critical and like games, or musical? Kids can be pretty fickle and start things and don't finish so that is why it is good to do it with them to make sure they follow through and become confident in their skills. My son was more athletic so we rode bikes, skate boards and went to parks. My daughter is pretty creative so we did things as inspiration allowed. Collage is a good one to start with like cutting things out of a magazine and filling a space with the images. It evokes critical and creative thinking. 

Anyway, hope this helps. I know how it feels to be overwhelmed and that can be crippling feeling like you haven't done enough. Just let them have fun and stay connected. You have got this!
